newsitem.title: USA: Vote on N.J. pension bonds not on calendar - paper.
newsitem.headline: Vote on N.J. pension bonds not on calendar - paper.

text.p: Although the New Jersey Legislature has another chance this week to consider a $2.8 billion pension bond deal, neither the Assembly nor the Senate have scheduled a vote, the Bergen Record reported Monday.
Both houses postponed votes on the measure in March and April when they previously considered it, because lawmakers were unable to muster enough support.
The plan put forward by the Whitman administration is to sell $2.75 billion of bonds and use the proceeds toward paying off the state's unfunded pension liability.
The move would also allow the state to avoid making scheduled 1997 and 1998 payments into the system, freeing up about $600 million to help balance the budget.
